title: Impact of M&A Announcements on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Event Study.  
Rationale: Merger announcements are sharp, well-timed information shocks. By comparing actual returns in a short “event window’’ to a firm-specific expected return generated from a pre-event “estimation window’’ (market-model), we difference out normal movements and isolate the causal effect of the announcement.

Key assumptions  
• Market efficiency: prices immediately incorporate new information, so abnormal returns within the window are attributable to the announcement.  
• No confounding news in the same window.  
• Stationary return-generation process between estimation and event windows (α and β are stable).  
• Independence of firms’ error terms (for classical t-tests).  

---

## 2. R Code
```r
###############################################
# Event–study: M&A announcement abnormal returns
###############################################
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(broom)
library(tidyr)

# 1. Read data -------------------------------------------------------------
file_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s52_data.csv"
dat <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# 2. Windows --------------------------------------------------------------
est_win  <- -250:-30     # estimation window
evt_win  <-  -1:1        # main event window  (-1,0,+1)
rob_win  <-  -5:5        # robustness window  (-5 … +5)

# 3. Market-model coefficients (α, β) -------------------------------------
betas <- dat %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% est_win) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  do(tidy(lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = .))) %>% 
  select(stock_id, term, estimate) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = estimate) %>% 
  rename(alpha = `(Intercept)`, beta = mkt_ret)

# 4. Abnormal returns ------------------------------------------------------
dat_mm <- dat %>% 
  left_join(betas, by = "stock_id") %>% 
  mutate(exp_ret = alpha + beta * mkt_ret,
         ar      = ret  - exp_ret)

# 5. CAR (-1,1) ------------------------------------------------------------
car_main <- dat_mm %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% evt_win) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise(CAR = sum(ar, na.rm = TRUE), .groups="drop")

mean_car  <- mean(car_main$CAR, na.rm = TRUE)
t_stat    <- mean_car / (sd(car_main$CAR)/sqrt(nrow(car_main)))
p_value   <- 2*pt(-abs(t_stat), df = nrow(car_main)-1)

cat("\n========== Main result ==========\n")
cat(sprintf("Average CAR (-1,1):  %6.4f\n", mean_car))
cat(sprintf("t-statistic:          %6.2f  (p = %.4f)\n", t_stat, p_value))

# 6. Robustness 1: wider window (-5,5) ------------------------------------
car_rob <- dat_mm %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% rob_win) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise(CAR = sum(ar, na.rm = TRUE), .groups="drop")

mean_car2 <- mean(car_rob$CAR, na.rm = TRUE)
t_stat2   <- mean_car2 / (sd(car_rob$CAR)/sqrt(nrow(car_rob)))
p_value2  <- 2*pt(-abs(t_stat2), df = nrow(car_rob)-1)

cat("\nRobustness: CAR (-5,5)\n")
cat(sprintf("Average CAR: %6.4f | t = %5.2f | p = %.4f\n",
            mean_car2, t_stat2, p_value2))

# 7. Robustness 2: constant-mean model ------------------------------------
mu_hat <- dat %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% est_win) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise(mu = mean(ret, na.rm = TRUE), .groups="drop")

car_const <- dat %>% 
  left_join(mu_hat, by = "stock_id") %>% 
  mutate(ar = ret - mu) %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% evt_win) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise(CAR = sum(ar, na.rm = TRUE), .groups="drop")

mean_car3 <- mean(car_const$CAR, na.rm = TRUE)
t_stat3   <- mean_car3 / (sd(car_const$CAR)/sqrt(nrow(car_const)))
p_value3  <- 2*pt(-abs(t_stat3), df = nrow(car_const)-1)

cat("\nRobustness: Constant-mean model (-1,1)\n")
cat(sprintf("Average CAR: %6.4f | t = %5.2f | p = %.4f\n",
            mean_car3, t_stat3, p_value3))
```

---

## 3. Expected Findings  
Historical evidence shows targets earn strongly positive abnormal returns (~10 % over a few days) while acquirers experience small gains or slight losses. Because this file pools 100 firms without distinguishing roles, the cross-sectional average CAR over (-1, 1) should still be positive but muted—roughly +1 % (0.01) with a t-stat around 3–4, statistically significant. The wider window should remain positive, though slightly smaller per-day (≈ +1.5 % over (-5, 5)).

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: We compare stock returns around the announcement day to assess abnormal performance.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The merger announcement leads to a positive abnormal return.
